kept.excerpt: An Atlas/Focus poll published on September 21 put Elmano de Freitas at 48.5% and Ciro Gomes at 48% in the first round. In a hypothetical runoff, Elmano had 49.7% and Ciro 49.4%. The survey interviewed 1,815 Ceará voters through random digital recruitment between September 15 and 20, with a margin of error of two percentage points and 95% confidence. Its electoral registration numbers were CE-02298/2026 and BR-05493/2026.
kept.relevance: The latest eligible poll places the two leading candidates essentially level in both rounds immediately before the evidence cutoff.

kept.excerpt: A Real Time Big Data poll published on September 18 showed Elmano de Freitas with 47% and Ciro Gomes with 42% in the stimulated first-round scenario. In a hypothetical runoff, Elmano had 48% and Ciro 45%. The institute interviewed 1,600 voters between September 14 and 17, with a margin of error of two percentage points and 95% confidence. The poll was registered with the TSE under CE-04380/2026.
kept.relevance: This recent independent survey provides evidence of an Elmano numerical lead while showing a runoff advantage within the reported margin of error.

kept.excerpt: A Datafolha poll released on September 18 showed Ciro Gomes with 47% of voting intentions and Elmano de Freitas with 40%. In the previous Datafolha survey, released on September 3, Ciro had 46% and Elmano 37%. The latest survey interviewed 1,204 voters aged 16 or older between September 14 and 17.
kept.relevance: A major pollster shows Ciro ahead during the same fieldwork period as a survey favoring Elmano, making disagreement between polling institutes material to the forecast.

kept.excerpt: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on September 18 showed Ciro Gomes with 47.4% and Elmano de Freitas with 39.9% in the first round. The survey interviewed 1,352 people between September 15 and 17. Its margin of error was 2.7 percentage points at a 95% confidence level, and its TSE registration was CE-04259/2026.
kept.relevance: Another recent polling institute reports a substantial Ciro lead, providing a counterweight to the Atlas tie and Real Time Big Data results favoring Elmano.

kept.excerpt: An Ipsos-Ipec release dated June 3 reported Ciro Gomes at 44% and Elmano de Freitas at 33% of first-round voting intentions. Fieldwork took place between May 28 and June 1, 2026. The survey conducted 800 in-person interviews across 37 municipalities.
kept.relevance: This primary polling release supplies an earlier campaign baseline against which the tighter September readings can be assessed, allowing for differences between institutes and candidate scenarios.

kept.excerpt: The electoral calendar established by TSE Resolution 23.760 schedules the 2026 elections for October 4, including the election of state governors. The second round is scheduled for October 25. Parties and federations hold candidate-selection conventions between July 20 and August 5.
kept.publisher: Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Santa Catarina
kept.relevance: This dated official electoral-court publication confirms the election timetable and the time remaining from the forecasting cutoff to voting.

kept.excerpt: Elmano de Freitas of the Workers' Party was elected governor of Ceará in the first round of the 2022 election. He ran for the Ceará Cada Vez Mais Forte coalition, which included the PT-led federation, PP, MDB, PRTB, the PSOL federation and Solidariedade. His running mate was Jade Romero.
kept.relevance: Official historical reporting establishes Elmano's prior electoral victory and coalition background as context for his incumbency in the 2026 contest.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-09-21, inclusive; Q101 concerns the Ceará gubernatorial election. Included seven sources with explicit publication dates on or before the cutoff. Excerpts are factual English translations or paraphrases of the Portuguese source text. Dates and article content were verified through web_search results; web_fetch failed because multiple providers were registered, and the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so direct full-page retrieval was unavailable. Folha reports a same-day update on September 18; the TSE historical article reports an update on July 8, 2026, both before the cutoff. The TSE's main 2026 calendar news page was excluded because it displayed an update after the cutoff; an eligible regional electoral-court publication was used instead. Unknown-date aggregators, later reporting, election outcomes, and prediction-market or betting sources were excluded. Polls from different institutes are retained separately and are not treated as directly comparable measures of change.
